To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured 51 subarcsec binary orbits to 0.1 mas precision, discovered 5 new astrometric companions, and measured 2 triple star orbits.
the PHASES data are the most precise measurements ever made of 51 subarcsec binaries, with the exception of the binary stars that have been observed by the Hubble Space Telescope.
we have measured the orbital motions of several binaries with high precision, and we have discovered a faint astrometric companion to a binary system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the astrometric detection of extrasolar planets, (2) the determination of the orbits of nearby subarcsecond binary stars and the study of their orbital parameters and physical properties, (3) the determination of orbits of nearby subparsec triple and quadruple systems to determine their geometries, and (4) the study of the orbital dynamics of nearby subarcminute systems.
the study of the dynamics of stellar systems, and in particular the formation and orbital properties of multiple star systems and their relation to the formation and properties of planets.
the measurement and interpretation of high-precision astrometric measurements of binary stars.

the PTI astrometric precision was 0.5 mas, the Keck AO photometry precision was 1 mmag, and the PTI-Keck AO photometry was 0.1 mmag.
we have measured the relative astrometric positions of 51 stars to an accuracy better than 0.2 mas.
the PHASES data archive is a unique resource for astrometry, astrophysics, and exoplanet science.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PTI astrometric measurements are highly accurate and precise, with the median uncertainty in the position angle of a target star of 0.3 mas.
the PTI data are of high quality and can be used to determine high-precision astrometric orbits.
the PHASES targets are excellent candidates for direct imaging searches for faint astrometric and/or spectroscopic companions.
